 'This 100 is for you!': Litton Das turns daughter's birthday into a special occasion with emotional celebration

(Pic credit: Litton Das' FB post) Litton Das gave his daughter Anayra a birthday present to cherish, celebrating her special day with a magnificent century against South Africa in the first Test at the Wanderers in Johannesburg. Unable to be with his little princess on her birthday, the Bangladesh batter found a special way to make the occasion memorable, dedicating his eighth Test hundred to her with a handwritten message that brought a personal touch to his fighting knock. After reaching the three-figure mark on the second morning, Das pulled out a handwritten note from his pocket and held it up for the cameras. The message read: "Happy Birthday to my Princess. This 100 is for you!" Watch Shreyas Iyer on India's series win, bowling brilliance, captaincy challenges and more It was an emotional moment for the Bangladesh batter, who had already expressed his love for his daughter through a heartfelt social media post ahead of the occasion. "Happy Birthday, my princess! I wish I could be with you on your special day, but even from afar, you are always in my thoughts and prayers. My blessings are with you, today and always. May you always be blessed with good health, happiness, and a beautiful heart. Grow up to be a wonderful person and keep shining, my little one. Your dad loves you more than words can ever express." The century was particularly special as Das had to overcome a difficult situation to put Bangladesh in a commanding position after their top order had collapsed on the opening day. Litton, Hridoy script remarkable Bangladesh recovery
 Bangladesh were in deep trouble after opting to bat, with Kagiso Rabada ripping through their top order to reduce the visitors to 22/3 inside nine overs. The South African fast bowler dismissed debutant Mahfijul Islam, Mominul Haque and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto to put the hosts firmly in control. Towhid Hridoy and Tanzid Hasan then attempted to stabilise the innings with a 99-run partnership. Tanzid contributed 67 off 108 balls before Rabada struck again, removing him and Mushfiqur Rahim in quick succession. Bangladesh were 121/5 when Das joined Hridoy. What followed was a magnificent counterattack. The two batters stitched together a 206-run partnership for the sixth wicket, completely changing the complexion of the innings. Hridoy continued his impressive run in Test cricket, scoring 137 off 227 deliveries for his second century in just seven innings. He had struck a remarkable 224 against the West Indies recently. Das, meanwhile, brought up his half-century off 71 balls and finished the opening day unbeaten on 92. He needed only a few overs on Monday to complete his eighth Test century, becoming just the third Bangladesh batter to score a Test hundred against South Africa. Join conversation

 He eventually departed for 120 off 179 balls, an innings featuring 14 fours and a six, after pulling Dane Paterson towards mid-wicket, where Marco Jansen completed the catch. Litton Das' special celebration after scoring hundred. (Pic credit: Litton Das' FB post) Paterson leads South Africa's fightback
 Despite the resistance from Das and Hridoy, South Africa managed to bowl Bangladesh out for 400 before lunch on the second day. Paterson was the pick of the bowlers, claiming four wickets for 92 runs, while Rabada finished with five for 51. Jansen chipped in with two wickets. South Africa began their reply cautiously but suffered an early setback when Aiden Markram was caught behind off Hasan Mahmoud for four. The hosts were 18/1 at lunch.
